newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA SAYS COULD BE KEY INTERNET COUNTRY.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA SAYS COULD BE KEY INTERNET COUNTRY.

text.p: Australia is well placed to enjoy economic growth and job creation from the Internet, Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Wednesday.
"In many ways, Australia is very well placed to be a world leader (in the on-line industry)," Alston told reporters after giving an address at the Internet World '97 conference here.
"It has many comparative advantages that are the envy of most countries in our region," he said.
"If we build on those, we will be able to turn this into a major area for economic growth and job creation."
Under pressure from business to take a more active industry policy, Australia's conservative government has recently cited the information sector as a key source of job creation.
Prime Minister John Howard, during a recent tour of the United States, was impressed by the contribution the on-line industry had played in the revival of the U.S. economy.
Alston said in his speech that employment in Australia's information technology industry was to grow to 650,000 by the year 2000, from around 500,000 currently.
While employment in the country's telecommunications sector had grown to 95,000 in February 1997 from 80,000 in August 1994, Alston said.
The growth of the Internet, on-line services and the telecommunications, would mean further job growth in these areas, the minister said.
